original_text: 5.2 Application lifecycle [Lifecycle-01] The MEC host shall be available for the hosting of MEC applications. [Lifecycle-02] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host within the MEC system. [Lifecycle-03] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host when required by the operator.

attribute_scores.rationale: Terms like 'MEC host', 'MEC management', and 'instantiation' are defined in the domain, though 'available' could be more precisely bounded.
Lacks specific preconditions and failure/error handling scenarios when instantiation fails or the host is unavailable.
Terminology aligns properly with ETSI MEC glossary and standards.
Uses the mandatory modal verb 'shall' and follows subject-action structure, but crams multiple tagged statements into a single block.
Technically realistic and standard for cloud and edge computing orchestration frameworks.
The requirement block contains three distinct, tagged requirements ([Lifecycle-01], [Lifecycle-02], [Lifecycle-03]) bundled into a single text entry.
Testing instantiation and host availability is feasible, but lacks concrete quantitative performance or timing criteria.

shortcomings.problematic_excerpt: [Lifecycle-01] The MEC host shall be available for the hosting of MEC applications. [Lifecycle-02] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host within the MEC system. [Lifecycle-03] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host when required by the operator.
shortcomings.explanation: Multiple distinct requirements with separate lifecycle tags are combined into a single requirement entry. Each distinct requirement should be specified independently.
Conditionals like 'when required by the operator' lack specifications regarding the interface, mechanism, or authentication required by the operator to trigger this action.

layer1.document_understanding_summary: The requirement specifies the foundational lifecycle responsibilities within the ETSI Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) framework, focusing on host availability and management-driven application instantiation.

evaluations.original_problematic_excerpt: [Lifecycle-01] The MEC host shall be available for the hosting of MEC applications. [Lifecycle-02] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host within the MEC system. [Lifecycle-03] The MEC management shall support the instantiation of an application on a MEC host when required by the operator.
evaluations.context_reasoning: While multiple tags ([Lifecycle-01], [Lifecycle-02], [Lifecycle-03]) are used within the text, they form a cohesive functional grouping defining the fundamental application lifecycle capabilities of the MEC host and management. Treating them together under clause 5.2 is standard for ETSI specifications and does not impair testing or implementation.

The phrase 'when required by the operator' refers to high-level system capabilities. Detailed interfaces, authentication mechanisms, and API triggers are fully specified in subsequent reference point protocol specifications (e.g., Mp1, Mm3) of the ETSI MEC architecture, making this omission acceptable at this architectural layer.

layer2.reasoning_summary: DEF-1 is discarded because combining related sub-clauses under a single structured requirement heading is a common and acceptable document convention in ETSI standards, provided they share a thematic scope (Application lifecycle). DEF-2 is discarded because interface, mechanism, and authentication details for operator-triggered actions are architectural specifications covered by lower-level reference point (Mp1/Mp2/Mm3) protocol specifications rather than high-level functional requirements.
